subject: [RFC PATCH v3] mm/cma: don't release CMA pages still in use

reviews.author: David Hildenbrand (Arm)
reviews.summary: Identified a potential issue with the patch's implementation, suggesting that it may not be robust enough to handle buggy drivers. Proposed an alternative approach using page_ref_freeze() to consistently leak all pages.

2026-08-20.patch_summary: This patch series proposes a change to the Contiguous Memory Allocator (CMA) code in the Linux kernel. The goal is to prevent CMA pages from being released prematurely when they are still in use by a device. This can lead to double-queueing and corruption of buddy lists. The patch introduces a new check to ensure that a CMA region is not freed if any of its pages are still referenced.
